articles.title: ONE Fight Night 47 MMA And Submission Grappling Results: Henrique, Jaworski, Dantas, And Aragon Stun In Bangkok
articles.summary: Here's what went down in all the MMA and submission grappling matches at ONE Fight Night 47!
articles.body:
The world's largest martial arts organization returned to U.S. primetime with ONE Fight Night 47: Stamp vs. Flores , which aired live from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, September 4, and the card's MMA and submission grappling action delivered absolute fireworks.

Not only were fans treated to a pair of highlight-reel submission victories, but they also witnessed two competitive battles that went the distance and saw momentum swing back and forth multiple times.

Before we move on to the blockbuster main event, here is everything that went down in the MMA and submission grappling matches at ONE Fight Night 47.

Henrique Grinds Out Kurosawa For Decision Win

Brazilian juggernaut Fabio "The Giant" Henrique put himself on a two-bout winning streak, as he defeated Ryohei Kurosawa by unanimous decision in their strawweight MMA bout, which featured everything from wild exchanges inside the pocket to near-finishing submission attempts.

Henrique cracked the Japanese combatant with a spinning backfist in round one, sending the 33-year-old tumbling to the canvas. The 34-year-old Brazilian followed him to the ground and looked to finish with punches, but Kurosawa showed the durability of titanium. He returned to his feet, as both men spent the rest of the stanza trading fiery shots.

Kurosawa came out swinging in round two, unloading a whirlwind of punches and accidentally poking Henrique in the eye. The Brazilian hung tough, however, and he later brought the action back to the canvas and punished his rival with ground strikes.

Both men traded hooks in the third and final round, but soon, "The Giant" took the fight back to the mat. There, he slammed punches and knees into Kurosawa's face until the Japanese veteran gave up his back. Henrique locked in an arm-triangle choke but could not force the tap before the horn sounded.

With the victory, Henrique improved his record to 16-2 and carries momentum with two straight victories in the world's largest martial arts organization.

Jaworski Shocks Lovato Jr. With Kneebar Submission

In the battle of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu World Champions, Pawel Jaworski emerged victorious.

Jaworski, an IBJJF No-Gi World Champion, forced four-time BJJ World Champion Rafael Lovato Jr. to tap out from a lateral kneebar at the 1:51 mark of their middleweight submission grappling bout.

The 22-year-old Polish star locked up with Lovato Jr. early, but he eventually climbed onto his back and suffocated him with a tangle of arms and legs, clinging to him like an octopus latched onto its prey as he hunted for submissions.

Jaworski then shimmied around to the front, but the 43-year-old Oklahoma resident slammed him to the canvas in an attempt to break free of the grip. The Polish dynamo, who made his middleweight debut, was not deterred though. He hung on tight and then transitioned smoothly into the lateral kneebar that forced the tap.

The stunning finish earned Jaworski a US$50,000 bonus and moved his career record to 44-8.

Dantas Outlasts Almonacid In Back-And-Forth War

Brazilian sensation Pedro "Guerreiro" Dantas outworked Argentine promotional newcomer Hector "La Araña" Almonacid to score a unanimous decision victory in their featherweight MMA bout.

Dantas took control in the opening stanza, picking his shots from the outside with low kicks and long punches. Almonacid closed the distance with the clinch, where he accidentally landed a low blow.

Once the action resumed, the 23-year-old from Guerreiros Team landed some solid knees to the body, stuffed the Argentine's takedown attempts, put him on the ground, and unloaded some effective ground-and-pound.

The Brazilian survived an early scare in the second. After bringing his rival down with a modified ninja choke, Almonacid escaped and returned to his feet. Then, he landed a double-leg takedown, slid into full mount, and rained down punches. However, Dantas brilliantly reversed course and got inside his 24-year-old foe's guard, where he dished out some blows of his own.

Almonacid once again scored a takedown and secured full mount in the third round, where he punished "Guerreiro" with punches until the Brazilian gave up his back. "La Araña" unsuccessfully searched for a rear-naked choke, and once more, Dantas reversed course, reclaimed top position, and closed out the fight with more ground-and-pound.

The back-and-forth battle went the distance, with the judges siding unanimously with Dantas. That victory – the first in ONE Championship for the Brazilian – upped his record to 7-1.

Aragon Submits Fujimoto With Scarf-Hold Americana

Macarena Aragon returned to the winner's circle in highlight-reel fashion, as she submitted Japanese-Brazilian rising star Gabi Fujimoto via scarf-hold Americana in the third and final round of their atomweight MMA contest.

Aragon set the tone early, as she tied her opponent up in the corner, exchanged clinch knees, and then hip-tossed her to the canvas, where she began setting up the scarf hold and hunting for submissions.

The pair traded knees in the clinch during the second stanza, but the Argentine once again dragged the fight to the mat, where she dominated with submission attempts and ground strikes.

Aragon picked up where she left off in the final canto, as she brought her foe back to the canvas and eventually locked in the scarf-hold Americana to force the tap at the 2:06 mark of round three.

That finish capped a decisive grappling performance for Aragon, who scored her sixth professional win.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Predictions for Irish icon's farewell fight from fighters and pundits
articles.summary: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Katie Taylor's farewell fight against Flora Pili in Dublin on Saturday. .
articles.body:
Katie Taylor brings the curtain down on a remarkable career on Saturday when she faces unbeaten Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park in Dublin.

Taylor is an Olympic gold medallist and two-weight undisputed champion who has won 25 of her 26 professional fights, with six victories by stoppage.

The 40-year-old has long dreamed of fighting at Croke Park and will finally get her wish in the final bout of her career.

French challenger Pili, 29, is undefeated in 12 professional contests, with two stoppage wins. She is former European champion, but has never faced anyone with Taylor's pedigree or experience.

Victory in the light-welterweight contest would provide a fairytale ending for one of Ireland's greatest sporting careers and see Taylor become an undisputed champion for a third time.

Can Taylor produce one final vintage performance on the biggest night of her career?

Or will the younger, unbeaten Pili spoil the occasion and pull off a mammoth upset?

BBC Sport spoke to figures from the boxing world to get their predictions for Saturday's fight.

Tony Bellew - former cruiserweight world champion

"Saturday is the perfect tribute to probably the greatest female boxer that has ever lived in Katie Taylor. Flora Pili has the perfect style that will make Katie Taylor look great.

"It'll be a brilliant night and it will be capped off with a fantastic performance from Katie Taylor."

Ellie Scotney - former undisputed super-bantamweight champion

"100% Katie Taylor wins. It will be a night where she captures the hearts of not just Ireland but so many nations. She is the purest of souls and that is so much more of boxing. I pray that when she leaves that ring she knows what she has done for the people who will come through in boxing."

Anthony Crolla - former lightweight world champion

"I think we see Katie rolling back the years and one more Katie Taylor performance. I wouldn't be surprised if we saw a late stoppage and capped an unbelievable career. She will get a homecoming fit for a queen.

"I'm very jealous I'm not there but I'm not ruling out getting a flight there and doing an all-nighter and getting the 6am flight back home."

Alycia Baumgardner - unified super-featherweight champion

"Katie Taylor is going to have an amazing performance and this is what she's wanted at Croke Park. Taylor will give it her all during her last rodeo and will put on an amazing performance to get the win."

Carl Frampton - former two-weight world champion

"I've watched bits of Pili and she looks OK, but Katie is on a different level and should win, will win. It will be the icing on the cake for Katie to end a career that we may never see again from a fighter from these shores.

"It's a little harder for the women to get stoppages with the two-minute rounds, but I feel Katie may well find a finish in the later rounds."

Coverage on Radio 5 Sports Extra from 19:00 BST, then 5 Live from 22:00. Ringwalks for main event expected between 22:00 and 22:30.

Michael Conlan - world title challenger and former world amateur champion

"It's going to be a very special evening and I think Katie wins by mid-to-late stoppage. She's always been one to rise to the occasion and with this being her swansong, I think she will put on an unbelievable performance on an unbelievable night.

"There will be plenty of tears shed in Croke Park and I can't wait to witness the greatest ever athlete our country has produced, male or female, go out in style."

Barry Jones - former super-featherweight world champion

"It will be a great send off for the great Katie Taylor. I don't think Katie will have too much trouble with Flora Pili, who is decent but I think she will be overawed with the pressure and the combination punches.

"Katie rarely gets a stoppage but I think she will this time. It's a clear win and she can sail off into the sunset as the greatest female boxer there has ever been."

"Katie Taylor has her dream opportunity as she closes her unprecedented career. She has been the pioneer, standout female fighter and jewell in the Emerald Isle.

"Flora Pili will do her very best but I think Katie will come through to win, claim the undisputed title and bow out in style."

"Boxing always has this way of throwing a curve ball, there's always a banana skin somewhere and this might be it.

"Katie Taylor hasn't fought for nearly a year-and-a-half when she had the trilogy with Amanda Serrano. She's 40-years-old, there's a lot of wear and tear and mileage on her. The same can't be said for Pili. She's fought a few levels down but she's unbeaten and will come with confidence.

"I think Katie will get it done but don't think it will be without problems, so Taylor to get it done on a close decision."

articles.title: Andy Ruiz Jr: Ex-world champion loses to Poland's Damian Knyba
articles.summary: American heavyweight Andy Ruiz Jr, who shocked Anthony Joshua in 2019 to take his world titles, loses comeback fight to Poland's Damian Knyba.
articles.body:
Former world champion Andy Ruiz Jr has vowed to carry on after losing his comeback fight to Poland's Damian Knyba in New Jersey.

The 36-year-old heavyweight shocked the boxing world seven years ago by beating Britain's Anthony Joshua to take his world titles.

Ruiz Jr has since been beset by injuries and was taking part in just his fourth fight since losing the rematch to Joshua in December 2019.

He looked a shadow of his former self at the Prudential Center in Newark, saved by the bell after scrambling back to his feet following a knockdown in the seventh, he eventually lost by a unanimous points decision.

Judges scored the fight 117-110, 114-113 and 114-113 in favour of the Pole, who took his record to 18 wins and one defeat, but Ruiz Jr was quick to demand a rematch.

"I don't know, I think it was just him holding," said Ruiz Jr, who recently signed up with British promoter Eddie Hearn.

"Every time I tried to come in, he'd hold me really tight, and I just couldn't let my combinations go.

"He played a good game plan, but I'd love to run it back and do things a lot different."

Joshua's former conqueror argued that he was simply rusty after taking his first fight since drawing with American Jarrell Miller in August 2024.

"It was just a long layoff, and it was a great opponent," he argued.

"I didn't want to take an easy fight, so that's why I took Damian. He's a big guy. But we've got to take risks. I've still got it in me, man. I've just got to stay active and I want to fight again."

articles.title: Anthony Joshua: Heavyweight's former trainer has his say on what happens next in Tyson Fury fight negotiations
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have been negotiating a blockbuster showdown later this year; Fury has "signed up" for the fight and is "just waiting for AJ", says his promoter Frank Warren; Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn says talks have "reopened" to stage the fight at Wembley Stadium
articles.body:
Frank Warren, who promotes Fury, told Sky Sports this week that terms were agreed and they were "waiting for AJ", while Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has announced that talks have reopened to stage the fight at Wembley Stadium .

But McCracken, who trained Joshua as an amateur and steered him to world heavyweight title glory as a professional, believes the two British stars should not pay any attention to the constant speculation about a long-awaited fight.

"I had a career as a fighter and you look back at what you maybe wished you should have done and what you shouldn't have done," McCracken exclusively told Sky Sports .

"I think it works out how it should work out most of the time, but it's up to the fighters if they want to fight each other and try and get the better of each other.

"I don't think it's anybody else's business whether they should fight or not - I think they both proved themselves.

"One thing I'd say is everyone's talking about it - it puts boxing on the map and it's great for boxing. While boxing's in the forefront and in the news, I think it's a really positive thing."

Fury expressed his frustration at the prolonged negotiations in a social media outburst, branding Joshua as a "coward" , but McCracken insists the Olympic gold medallist and former world champion would relish the chance to settle a fierce rivalry.

"With Anthony Joshua, in my experiences, he was happy to fight anybody," said McCracken. "It was just about how it was packaged and what was best for him - that's how the fighters look at things these days.

"I've not been involved for a long time with Joshua, but it looks like it's going to happen. Hopefully it will and then obviously everyone can enjoy it."

The fighters had differing fortunes in summer warm-up fights as Fury sealed a one-sided stoppage of Mariusz Wach, while Joshua had to climb off the canvas twice before halting Kristian Prenga.

But McCracken has suggested that Joshua will be fuelled by the criticism of his close scare.

He said: "Joshua is coming off the back of not a great performance, but obviously he got the knockout and that is all that really matters. He'll be looking to prove people wrong, any of the doubters.

"Tyson [Fury] would be the favourite at the moment with his recent results and his form. It's quite fascinating if you actually think about it, where it's got to and the time it's taken to actually get the fight on."

'A Night of Solidarity' - Olympic-style night to celebrate power of sport

McCracken was speaking to Sky Sports ahead of 'A Night of Solidarity' on November 13, a night of Olympic-style boxing to celebrate the unifying power of sport and raise funds for firefighters' charities, youth sport organisations and community groups in North Kensington.

The night has been created to recognise the actions of the local community in the aftermath of the Grenfell Tower tragedy, when local boxing and sports clubs came together to help the community rebuild, create safe spaces for young people and help everyone affected by this devastating event.

The London Fire Brigade Boxing Club (LFB) has worked with local communities across London to deploy the unifying power of sport to provide structure and purpose to the lives of young people, bringing them together with rank-and-file firefighters in boxing gyms in a show of solidarity and support.

'A Night of Solidarity' aims to celebrate both these endeavours and bring them together, recognising the important role played by both the LFB Boxing Club and those clubs in the areas most impacted by the Grenfell Tower fire.

The evening will raise funds for local sports charities, the Firefighter's Charity and will include 12 bouts of boxing that will see an LFB Select team take on a North Kensington team, made-up of men, women and youth boxers from a variety of clubs in the local area and across London.

articles.title: UFC Paris: Kurtis Campbell - from being bullied at school to the UFC
articles.summary: Introduced to combat sports as a seven-year-old after being bullied at school, Kurtis Campbell is now chasing success in the UFC.
articles.body:
Kurtis Campbell was only seven years old when his parents decided something drastically needed to change.

During his time at primary school in Liverpool, Campbell was targeted by bullies. His parents, Jay and Michelle, could see the effect it was having.

It was then that they signed him up for Muay Thai classes to help him learn how to defend himself.

"From there, I've never looked back," Briton Campbell told BBC Sport. "I've been in love with the sport ever since."

Without his parents' influence and support, the 24-year-old would not be chasing his dream of becoming a UFC champion.

Seventeen years later Campbell is preparing for his second fight in the promotion against American Trevor Peek at UFC Paris on Saturday.

"I'm not going to stop until my mum and dad are on a beach somewhere, sipping cocktails and doing nothing else for the rest of their lives," Campbell said.

"They can enjoy it, knowing that they've created this monster. That's my plan."

Initially, it seemed Campbell's time in the gym would serve the sole purpose of learning self-defence before moving to secondary school a couple of years later.

That was until he started competing in amateur competitions, slowly but surely becoming obsessed with his newfound escape from the difficulties he faced at school.

"I was quite a soft kid, in the sense that I didn't really like the violence or the fighting," Campbell said.

"I felt like when I did fight, and when I really did go into it, everything changed and I never looked back."

Aged 15, he won his first international Muay Thai title and started to realise that, with the blessing of his parents, combat sports could become more than just a pastime.

"I was never the cleverest kid. I was always in the bottom sets at school, so I wasn't really focused," Campbell said.

"All of the teachers told me, 'you need to do something else. You have to have a plan B.'"

But for Campbell, who was beginning to attract attention across Merseyside, his unwavering commitment to the sport meant there was no need for a back-up plan.

That included regularly running almost five miles to and from school. There was even one occasion when he missed school while studying for his GCSEs to attend a coaching seminar in Liverpool hosted by John Kavanagh - the coach of former two-weight UFC champion Conor McGregor.

After completing his GCSE exams at the age of 16, Campbell enrolled on a college course that combined studying for a qualification in sport with playing football.

Or at least that was what he was supposed to be doing.

Campbell struck an arrangement with the course leads that allowed him to attend classes before leaving to train in combat sports, while his peers were on the football pitch.

"I was always avoiding anything just for fighting," Campbell said.

"I really didn't like school. It wasn't me. But I made a good few mates there, so you've got to take the pros with the cons."

'That fat kid looking back at me would be proud'

When Campbell suffered a TKO defeat by Danny Silva on his UFC debut in March, it was the first time in almost seven and a half years that he had lost.

Not since December 2018, when he lost to fellow Liverpudlian Liam McCracken on the local amateur circuit, had featherweight Campbell failed to get his hand raised.

He won five titles across three different weight classes with the Full Contact Contender (FCC) promotion before earning a UFC contract on Dana White's Contender Series in September 2025.

It means that when he steps into the Accor Arena to fight Peek, he will face the unfamiliar feeling of trying to bounce back from defeat.

"Fighting in the UFC was just the goal and the dream when I was younger," Campbell said.

"So I feel like that fat kid looking back at me would be proud of me. I would be proud of myself, no matter how the debut went, just because of where I am now.

"I think he'd be happy with me. But I know he'd not be happy with just the story. I've still got a lot of legacy to build.

"That's one thing I would say is good and bad about me - as soon as I get something, I want more of it.

"I don't think I'll ever stop having that feeling."

articles.title: Andy Ruiz Jr loses comeback fight by unanimous decision but pledges to 'fight again'
articles.summary: Former heavyweight world champion Andy Ruiz Jr fell to a unanimous decision defeat in his first fight in over two years; Anthony Joshua’s former nemesis has struggled with injuries since his success seven years ago
articles.body:
Former heavyweight world champion Ruiz Jr, famous for stripping British boxer Anthony Joshua of his titles seven years ago, took on Poland's Knyba in New Jersey overnight on Friday.

The Mexican fell to a unanimous decision defeat in his first fight in two years, with the judges at the Prudential Center scoring the fight 117-110, 114-113 and 114-113.

Ruiz Jr hit the canvas in the seventh with his legs giving way and had to be saved by the bell, and despite late attempts to knock down Knyba, could not claw the fight back thanks to the Pole's disciplined approach.

The 36-year-old sported a black eye after the bout but Ruiz Jr - who has struggled with injury issues since his rematch defeat to Joshua in 2019 - is not letting the bruising defeat stop his comeback plan.

Ruiz Jr, who recently signed with Eddie Hearn's Matchroom, said: "It was just a long lay-off, and it was a great opponent.

"I didn't want to take an easy fight, so that's why I took Damian. He's a big guy. But we've got to take risks. I've still got it in me, man.

"I've just got to stay active and I want to fight again."

While Ruiz Jr continues to rebuild his career, Knyba will hope to bring himself into the world title mix, calling out German boxer and current WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel after his victory.

"I really want a rematch with Kabayel," he said.

Knyba was knocked out by Kabayel in Germany earlier this year.

articles.title: ONE Fight Night 47: Stamp Fairtex silences her doubts with defiant split-decision win over Selina Flores
articles.summary: Stamp Fairtex secured a split-decision victory in Bangkok; Thai fighter has been returning from serious injury and looks to have returned to her previous form, extending her winning streak to two
articles.body:
For months, she'd questioned whether her body - and more importantly, her mind - was ready. The meniscus tear that ravaged her knee in May 2024 had cast a shadow over every fight since. Hesitation had crept into her performances. Doubt had whispered in her ear.

However at ONE Fight Night 47, which aired live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Saturday morning from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium, the Thai megastar silenced those voices with a defiant split-decision victory over two-time WBC Muay Thai world champion Selina 'Teep Queen' Flores, proving she's ready to reclaim what she never stopped believing was hers.

From the opening bell, Stamp was willing to engage. She launched body kicks at Flores, pressured in the clinch, and drove knees upstairs with the precision of a surgeon. The American struggled to find her range at first. Her trademark teeps - the weapons that have made her dangerous - failed to materialise early on.

Flores grew into the second frame. Her low kicks began to find their mark. A sharp right hand cracked cleanly. The signature teep landed, and she finally found her rhythm. But Stamp met fire with fire, her counters arriving with timing that suggests the rust had genuinely fallen away.

The third round reached a crescendo and exploded into chaos. Flores had taken the lead, putting the Thai star on the back foot and often throwing first. Stamp comfortably played the counter game, repeatedly carving her shin into the American's body.

When the American threw a spinning back elbow that sailed past her rival, Stamp didn't hesitate - she flung one back and hit the target. A cartwheel kick followed, drawing roars from the crowd and a nod of respect from her rival. Even the 28-year-old from Pattaya couldn't help but grin from ear to ear.

In the end, the judges split their scorecards - and two of them were swayed by the Thai's output, giving her the win.

It may have been a razor-close victory, but for a fighter who was returning from a serious injury, had dropped a decision in her comeback fight last November, and admitted she had a poor showing in her last victory this past June, it was far more than that.

This was a performance that kept fans on the edge of their seats. The fighter herself was smiling and boldly taking risks on a previously injured leg that made her think twice over the past several months. It was vindication and proof that Stamp Fairtex was truly, finally, back.

Stamp - the first person to hold kickboxing, Muay Thai, and MMA gold in ONE Championship - improved her record to 66-18, and her winning streak extends to two. Whether she pursues the ONE Women's Atomweight MMA world title she relinquished in May 2025 or continues in Muay Thai next, one thing is for certain: she's ready.

articles.title: Katie Taylor Retirement Fight Odds, Live Stream and KO, Judges' Scorecards Predictions
articles.summary: Women's boxing star Katie Taylor is set to make her final walk to the ring on Saturday when she defends her undipsuted super lightweight title against Flora Pili at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland.
articles.body:
Women's boxing star Katie Taylor is set to make her final walk to the ring on Saturday when she defends her undipsuted super lightweight title against Flora Pili at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland.

Taylor's decorated career has included an Olympic gold medal, dominant title reigns and lightweight and super lightweight that included some of the biggest fights in the history of the sport.

Now, she gets the opportunity to close out her career on her terms in her home country against an undefeated contender.

Let's dive in and look at the details you need to catch the fight along with a preview.

Fight Odds, Schedule and Scorecard Prediction

When: Saturday, September 5 at 2 p.m. ET (main event ringwalks at approximately 5:10 p.m.)

Odds: Taylor -3000 ($3,000 bet to win $100); Pili +1320 ($100 bet wins $1,320)

Prediction: Taylor wins via unanimous decision (100-90x2, 99-91)

The stage is set for Taylor to take center stage once more, but this isn't exactly the best opponent she has seen. Pili is undefeated in 12 professional fights, but the quality of competition is reflected in the odds.

The Frenchwoman most recently claimed the IBO title with a majority decision over Jelena Janićijević. It was good enough to set her up with this opportunity. It just wasn't good enough to make her a viable threat.

Still, Taylor isn't overlooking her opponent as she looks to add one more statement victory to her resume.

"People have travelled all around the world to follow my career and I'm hoping I can repay some of that with a big performance on September 5," she told Matchroom Boxing . "I'm under no illusions that Flora will present a very tough challenge, she's undefeated as a professional and has a good amateur pedigree so I have the utmost respect for her."

Taylor, 40, is 11 years older than her opponent on Saturday night. However, she still should hold the advantage in hand speed, athleticism and talent.

Pili is a skilled boxer, but she doesn't pose much threat in the power department. She has finished just two of her 12 career wins. Taylor has been drawn into some fire fights in the later part of her career, but that shouldn't be a problem on Saturday.

The Croke Park crowd should get exactly what they are hoping for: A one-sided affair where the native daughter showcases her skills one last time.

articles.summary: 'El Potro Menorquín' se estrena con victoria por decisión unánime en la mejor liga de MMA del mundo
articles.body: Entrar por la puerta grande. Fabià Sintes (12-3) silenció el Accor Arena de París derrotando por decisión unánime al local Michael Aljarouj (13-4) en su estreno en UFC. 'El Potro Menorquín' controló los dos últimos asaltos y dejó una 'masterclass' de como controlar el combate en la lucha y en el suelo. Era el 'game plan'... y funcionó. Tras un primer asalto muy igualado en el que Aljarouj defendió bien los derribos del que fuera campeón del peso mosca de WOW... Sintes se impuso. Fabià encontró la forma de llevar a Aljarouj al suelo y lo destruyó en el segundo 'round' a base de codazos una vez lograda la posición en la montada. Aljarouj, pese a un arrebato de orgullo y carácter en el último minuto del combate, se desfondó y sucumbió ante la polivalencia y verstalidad de un Fabià que entra de la mejor forma posible en la mejor liga de MMA del mundo. Victoria fuera de casa, en Francia y ante un francés, para dejar su impronta y confirmar que se ha ganado de sobra su contrato con UFC.

articles.title: UFC Paris live results, highlights and play-by-play
articles.summary: UFC Paris results, highlights, live discussion and instant play-by-play, reactions and analysis.
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live THIS AFTERNOON (Sat., Sept. 5, 2026) with UFC Paris , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event happens at Accor Arena in Paris, France, featuring a special Octagon newcomer in the main event.

Salahdine Parnasse vs. Dan Hooker is our main event, going down in the Lightweight division. Parnasse is a long-time former KSW champion who made a big splash with his one and done appearance at MVP MMA . The reason he was done there was because UFC wanted to poach him out of that fledgling promotion before he drew too many serious mixed martial arts (MMA) fans over to it. Hooker comes into this one off two losses and looking very much like a sacrificial lamb. However, as last week taught us, -600 odds can be overcome .

The co-main is an all French affair, in the Featherweight division, with Fares Ziam meeting Axel Sola . Both of these guys are action fighters known for putting on a show. They should get the crowd roaring in Paris, even if it's not obvious to the locals whom they should be cheering for.

Rounding out the main card is Michael Page vs. Nursulton Ruziboev , Daniil Donchenko vs. Punahele Soriano , Kurtis Campbell vs. Trevor Peek and Losene Keita vs. Muhammad Naimov . Page might be trying to fight out of his UFC contract here, which is the reason UFC has pared him with a big, rangy striker who can also make you quit on the ground.

The featured "Prelim" is Morgan Charriere vs. Felipe Lima . The undercard also boasts Mario Pinto vs. Ryan Spann , Oumar Sy vs. Modestas Bukauskas and Nathaniel Wood against late replacement Pavel Andrusca . Further down the card we have Michael Aljarouj vs. Fabia Sintes , Nora Cornolle vs. Klaudia Sygula , Matthieu Duclos vs. Lucas Felipe Dias and Delphine Benouaich vs. Sofia Montenegro to make up the numbers. Aljarouj does look like an intriguing prospect, though.

We are operating at prime local time today. That means it is an extremely early wake up for me and anyone else on the east coast. Checkout these special air times below:

UFC Paris "Prelims" will begin at 12 p.m. ET .

UFC Paris main card is scheduled to start at 3 p.m. ET .

All of UFC Paris airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here .

The live blog here starts rolling below at 12 p.m. ET . Come in and say hi!

155 lbs.: Salahdine Parnasse vs. Dan Hooker

185 lbs.: Michael Page vs. Nursulton Ruziboev

145 lbs.: Kurtis Campbell vs. Trevor Peek

170 lbs.: Daniil Donchenko vs. Punahele Soriano

145 lbs.: Losene Keita vs. Muhammad Naimov

145 lbs.: Morgan Charriere vs. Felipe Lima

205 lbs.: Modestas Bukauskas def. Oumar Sy by TKO (punches), round 2 (3:57)

145 lbs.: Pavel Andrusca def. Nathaniel Wood by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

125 lbs.: Fabia Sintes def. Michael Alarouj by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-27)

135 lbs.: Nora Cornolle def. Klaudia Sygula by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

185 lbs.: Matthieu Duclos def. Luis Felipe Dias by TKO (check hook), round 1 (4:45) — HIGHLIGHTS

115 lbs.: Delphine Benouiach def. Sofia Montenegro by technical submission (rear naked choke), round 2 (4:22) — HIGHLIGHTS

Oumar Sy vs. Modestas Bukauskas: What a comeback? Sy dominated Bukauskas in the first round, pinning him down and coming close to a ground and pound finish. Bukauskas got up, though, at the urging of the referee and was able to survive. Turns out all that domination tired out Sy. In the second Bukauskas was able to get up quickly from a Sy takedown and then he turned up the pace, putting a beating on Sy on the feet. The tired Sy crumbled and Bakauskas was able to come away with a real gutsy win over Sy (whose time as a top prospect seems to be over).

Official decision: Modestas Bukauskas def. Oumar Sy by TKO (punches), round 2 (3:57)

Nathaniel Wood vs. Pavel Andrusca : Wood looked good early on, stinging Andrusca with his striking. At that point Andrusca, a late replacement making his debut looked a little out of his depth. That might have just been Octagon jitters, though. As the fight went on he looked more comfortable and his wrestling started to give Wood a lot of problems. Andrusca was able to take Wood down and threaten with a submission in the second and then start beating him to the punch in the third. I scored it 29-28 for the newcomer.

Official decision: Pavel Andrusca def. Nathaniel Wood by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

Michael Alarouj vs. Fabia Sintes: Alarouj's striking looked nice in the first round, but his inability to stop a naked single leg takedown meant he spent far more of this fight on his back than he would have liked to. After a close opening round spent mainly on the feet, Sintes was able to suck up lots of control time in the second and third. Alarouj mounted a comeback in the third, but was unable to do any serious damage. I scored the fight for Sintes, to break France's winning streak.

Official decision: Fabia Sintes def. Michael Alarouj by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-27)

Nora Cornolle vs. Klaudia Sygula: The clinch was the story of this fight. Cornolle, the bigger body, was able to establish the clinch often in this fight and prevent Sygula from gaining an advantage through her better speed and volume striking. It wasn't pretty, but Cornolle did a good job of bullying Sygula around and getting a convincing decision.

Official decision: Nora Cornolle def. Klaudia Sygula by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Matthieu Duclos vs. Luis Felipe Dias: Another brawl! Dias might have been winning this one, landing plenty on Duclos as he blitzed forwards. He was very wild, though. Eventually he ran into a check hook and was briefly knocked out. He seemed to wake up when he hit the ground and was defending himself as the referee came in to break it up.

Official decision: Matthieu Duclos def. Luis Felipe Dias by TKO (check hook), round 1 (4:45)

Delphine Benouaich vs. Sofia Montenegro: that was a brutal start to the event. Benouaich and Montenegro throw down from the opening bell. Benouiach landed the cleaner shots early, but Montenegro's offense seemed to be wearing on her more. In the second, though, she landed a hard straight punch right to the jaw. That put down Montengro and Benouiach then split her open with brutal elbows. With Montenegro bleeding all over the place, Benouiach then took the back and choked her to sleep. Keep an eye on this girl!

Official decision: Delphine Benouiach def. Sofia Montenegro by technical submission (rear naked choke), round 2 (4:22)

articles.title: Valentina Shevchenko Vacates UFC Belt Due to Injury, New Title Fight Announced for UFC 332 Card
articles.summary: The UFC announced Saturday it will crown a new women's flyweight champion at UFC 332 on Oct. 3.
articles.body:
The UFC announced Saturday it will crown a new women's flyweight champion at UFC 332 on Oct. 3.

The promotion has vacated the title as Valentina Shevchenko is sidelined because of an injury. Natalia Silva will oppose Wang Cong in the main event.

Shevchenko regained the championship by winning a unanimous decision over Alexa Grasso in 2024. She then successfully defended the belt against Manon Fiorot and Zhang Weili.

The 38-year-old hasn't stepped inside the Octagon since last November, and that layoff will extend for an indeterminate period of time.

Silva is the No. 1 challenger in the UFC's official rankings . Wang, who's ranked sixth, is the major beneficiary of Shevchenko's exit as she now has the biggest fight of her MMA career ahead.

Wang is 10-1 as a pro and riding a four-fight winning streak. She was an experienced kickboxer before pivoting to mixed martial arts in 2022. Now, she's one win away from being a UFC champion.

Silva's overall record (20-5) is a little deceptive as to her recent dominance. Her last loss was nearly a decade ago. Since dropping a unanimous decision to Marina Rodriguez in December 2017, she has won 14 straight fights.

The main card for UFC 332 is slated to include a bantamweight battle between Deiveson Figueiredo and Payton Talbott along with a lightweight clash featuring King Green and Esteban Ribovics.

articles.title: Katie Taylor Retirement Fight vs. Flora Pili Judges' Scorecards, Punch Stats and Prize Money
articles.summary: Katie Taylor entered retirement in style with a unanimous decision victory over Flora Pili to become the undisputed super lightweight champion in front of a hometown crowd at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland.
articles.body:
Katie Taylor entered retirement in style with a unanimous decision victory over Flora Pili to become the undisputed super lightweight champion in front of a hometown crowd at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland.

Taylor wasted no time in establishing herself as the more dominant fighter. She put Pili on the defensive and peppered her with jabs to control the early rounds.

Pili was overwhelmed by Taylor's speed and skills, but Pili did put up enough offense to make a few moments interesting.

Those moments became fewer and farther between in the middle rounds. Taylor's speed was too much for Fili and she showed that she still had advantages despite the 11-year age gap.

Fellow women's boxing star Claressa Shields gave Taylor props for the strong performance.

Pili showed some life in the seventh round, forcing Taylor to show that she can still take a punch.

Taylor had more than enough chin to close out the fight as she continued to dominate the fight and end her career with a decisive win.

The win closes out one of the all-time great careers in women's boxing. Taylor was not only an Olympic gold medalist and two-division world champion, but her rivalry with Amanda Serrano blazed a new trail for women's boxing.

The first meeting between the two was the first women's fight to headline a card at Madison Square Garden. The rematch was the most-watched women's professional sporting event as the co-main event for Mike Tyson vs. Jake Paul on Netflix. The trilogy fight headlined the first ever all-women's card at Madison Square Garden.

Taylor parlayed dominant runs at lightweight and super lightweight into the high-profile trilogy with Serrano.

Serrano took to X to tip her cap to the champion.

Her hope is that her illustrious career will serve as inspiration for another generation of fighters.

"I've been blessed to achieve more than I could ever have dreamed in this sport but fighting at Croke Park really is the icing on the cake," she said, per Sky Sports . "I hope it's the kind of event that will inspire a whole new generation to take up sport and follow their passions - that for me would be the greatest legacy I could leave."

The Croke Park crowd didn't disappoint with its support for the Irish star.

With titles in multiple divisions and victories in a few of the biggest fights in the history of the sport, it's safe to say she's walking away from the sport as one of the all-time greats.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Ireland's boxing great crowns career in stylish Croke Park triumph
articles.summary: Katie Taylor ends illustrious career as a three-time undisputed world champion as Croke Park gave one of Ireland's greatest sporting figures the grandest of farewells.
articles.body:
Katie Taylor ended her illustrious career as a three-time undisputed world champion as Croke Park gave one of Ireland's greatest sporting figures the grandest of farewells on a night of celebration, spectacle and music.

The 40-year-old outclassed unbeaten Flora Pili on points in front of 80,000 jubilant fans to add the vacant WBC belt to her WBA, WBO and IBF light-welterweight titles.

With the footwork, speed and sharp pressure fighting that defined her career, Taylor produced one final stylish performance against the overmatched Frenchwoman to win by scores of 110-90, 110-90 and 98-91.

Promoter Eddie Hearn paid tribute to Taylor, calling her "Ireland's greatest sportsperson", before she took one final lap of the ring, waving to the crowd before ceremonially placing her gloves and belts in the centre of the canvas.

After almost a quarter of a century in the sport, Taylor - an Olympic champion, two-weight world champion and one of the pioneers of women's professional boxing - finally got her fairytale ending at her dream venue.

She bows out with a record of 26 wins and just one defeat, but this was about more than one final result.

It was a night steeped in Irish pride, with a spine-tingling atmosphere and chart-topping pop group Westlife helping provide a fitting send-off.

Taylor signs off career in style with unanimous decision win against Pili - reaction

On an unforgettable night for the city, around 80 per cent of those inside Croke Park had never previously attended a boxing event, but turned out to honour a fighter who dragged women's sport from the margins and took an entire nation on her journey.

The crowd was the sixth largest recorded post-war attendance for a boxing event anywhere in the world. By early evening, the stands were awash with green and white, tricolours draped over shoulders.

Westlife performed 'World of Our Own' and 'You Raise Me Up', with tens of thousands joining in as phone lights flickered around the towering tiers of Croke Park.

The atmosphere softened for an a cappella version of 'Grace', the well-known Irish ballad linked to the 1916 Easter Rising, before the national anthem rang out.

Chants of "Ole, Ole, Ole" drowned out Pili's ring-walk music before Taylor finally emerged to 'All Hail King Jesus', a nod to the faith she has spoken so openly about throughout her career.

She stretched her arms wide, sang along and tried to take in every second of her final walk to the ring. There was emotion on her face, but also the familiar focus as fireworks shot into the Dublin sky.

Taylor had spent fight week insisting there was still a job to do, but even for a fighter who had sold out Madison Square Garden and performed on some of boxing's grandest stages, it was hard to imagine her being untouched by a reception like this.

After a quiet opener, Taylor - Olympic champion at London 2012 and a professional since 2016 - burst into life in the second round, firing quick combinations before darting back out of range.

She repeatedly beat Pili to the punch, working in bursts and making the most of the two-minute rounds.

Pili, 29, arrived unbeaten in 12 contests and had previously held the European title. With little expectation on her shoulders, she had everything to gain.

But she had never faced anyone remotely close to Taylor's level and the gulf in class soon began to show.

The party atmosphere continued between rounds as it became increasingly clear there would be no gatecrashing from the Frenchwoman.

Former world champion Prince Naseem Hamed and UFC star Paddy Pimblett watched from ringside as Pili swung wildly in the fifth, only for Taylor to make her miss and fire back.

Pili enjoyed her best spell in the seventh, a quick flurry briefly snapping Taylor's head back, but it did little to alter the direction of the fight.

Croke Park rose for the final two minutes as Taylor continued to press forward, letting her hands go while the noise poured down from the stands.

She embraced her mother, trainer and manager in the ring as 'Celebration' rang around Croke Park before the inevitable result was read out.

"Let me just look around for a second", she said afterwards, soaking up every ounce of the reception.

'The greatest Irish sportsperson of all time'

Taylor has been unequivocal that Croke Park would be the end and she walks away having beaten every opponent she faced as a professional.

Her only defeat came against Chantelle Cameron in Dublin in 2023. Six months later, Taylor returned to the 3Arena and avenged it to become undisputed champion in a second weight division.

After the final bell, she paid tribute to her family and somehow held the tears back as she spoke to the crowd.

"There's nothing like an Irish mammy," she said, smiling as she thanked those closest to her.

For a fighter who has never hidden her dislike of media interviews, there was something striking about the confidence with which she walked around the ring, microphone in hand, soaking up the final moments.

Taylor will forever be defined by her trilogy wins against Amanda Serrano and leaves with a staggering list of accolades, but her true impact cannot be measured in statistics alone.

That legacy belongs to the young girl who once pretended to be a boy just to box when girls were not allowed.

She fought tirelessly to get the sport sanctioned in Ireland and included in the Olympics, before going on to conquer both the amateur and professional codes.

The belts will eventually gather dust, but the trail Taylor blazed across the sport will never fade.

articles.title: David Allen fight ends in bizarre fashion as Thomas Carty falls through ropes in round one on Katie Taylor undercard
articles.summary: Chief support bout for Katie Taylor's farewell fight was over in 82 seconds as Irish favourite, who was expected to win, tumbles through the ropes and is unable to continue; crowd jeered as incident was shown on Croke Park screens
articles.body:
The chief support for Katie Taylor's final fight before retirement was over after just 82 seconds with Carty - seeking the biggest win of his 12-bout career - unable to continue.

Allen caught Carty on the back of the head with a clubbing right hand and the Dublin southpaw tumbled through the ropes as much through momentum as the shot itself and onto the floor, where he was laid on his back.

After receiving medical attention - including oxygen for several minutes - Carty then walked back to the changing room and the fight was abandoned.

Allen, a 34-year-old journeyman from Doncaster, looked as bemused as the 80,000 crowd at the way the fight had ended.

The Irish fans booed as replays were shown on the giant screens and Allen was filmed saying: "That's one of the most bizarre things I've ever seen in my life."

Neither fighter spoke to the media immediately after the strange conclusion.

His last victory came over two years ago, when he defeated Mateusz Gamrot by split decision at UFC 305 in August 2024.

articles.body: El UFC París de este sábado no solo ha sido un éxito por la victoria de Fabià Sintes en su debut en la compañía, sino por una cartelera llena de nombres propios que han estado acompañadas de uno de los mejores públicos del mundo de las MMA. La guinda del pastel la ha puesto Salahdine Parnasse (24-2), que ha debutado a lo grande en la UFC frente a su gente noqueando a Dan Hooker (24-15) en el primer asalto y demostrando que el hype era real. La compañía tiene una nueva superestrella en peso ligero. La pelea tuvo poca historia. Parnasse llegaba con el cartel de doble campeón -y casi triple- de KSW y con el cartel de favorito directamente al combate estelar del evento. Algunos pensaban que era demasiado precipitado enfrentarle al número 11 de las 155 libras, pero esas dudas se disiparon con una patada al cuerpo, una patada a la cabeza y un gancho de izquierdas que tumbaron a 'Hangman' en un visto y no visto. Increíble. Ahora ha pedido a uno de sus ídolos, Max Holloway, y con esta actuación lo tiene más que merecido. Uno de los K.O. más impresionantes de la noche llegó en el evento co estelar. La UFC decidió enfrentar a Fares Ziam (18-6) con Axel Sola (13-1-1) en un derbi local que acabó con Sola noqueando brutalmente a Ziam en el primer asalto. En un golpe de encuentro cayó inconsciente y dejó al estadio silenciado durante unos segundos ante el aparatoso momento. Ya son tres victorias y tres finalizaciones para Axel desde su debut en la compañía hace un año, por lo que habrá que tenerle muy en cuenta en el futuro en peso ligero. El que tiene difícil su continuidad en la UFC es Michael Venom Page (26-3), que a pesar de vencer a Nursulton Ruziboev (37-10-2, 2NC) por decisión unánime ha vuelto a dejar muchas dudas con su actuación. Muchos gestos y pocos golpes que han provocado los pitos del público y que le dejan en una situación muy complicada dentro de la compañía a pesar de sumar cinco victorias y una derrota desde su llegada. El K.O. de la noche lo protagonizó Losene Keita (17-2), que tuvo un debut agridulce en la UFC con derrota a principios de año tras conseguir ser doble campeón en Oktagon. Sin embargo, se redimió de la mejor manera con un brutal derechazo a Muhammad Naimov (13-5) y una posterior celebración que fue aura pura. Ahora sí que ha llegado a la UFC. Otro que se redimió de su debut fue Kurtis Campbell (9-1), que sometió a Trevor Peek (9-4, 1NC) en el tercer asalto, mientras que Daniil Donchenko (16-2) continúa su ascenso en peso wélter tras vencer por decisión unánime a un duro rival como Punhaele Soriano (13-5). Lo siguiente seguramente sea un top 15 para él. La cartelera preliminar dejó luces y sombras para los peleadores franceses. Todo comenzó de buena manera con las finalizaciones de Delphine Benouaich (8-2) y Matthieu Duclos (11-3) y la victoria por decisión de Nora Cornolle (10-4) ante Claudia Sygula (8-3). Sin embargo, el clínic de Fabià Sintes (12-3) ante Michael Aljarouj (13-4, 2NC) torció todo. Por si fuera poco, Oumar Sy (12-3) volvió a dejar mucho que desear tras ser finalizado por Modestas Bukauskas (21-7) en el segundo asalto después de quedarse sin cardio. El mejor combate de las prelims lo protagonizaron Mario Pinto (13-0) y Ryan Spann (24-12). El peleador estadounidense estuvo a punto de noquear -y más tarde someter- al portugués en los primeros compases de la pelea, pero Pinto se repuso para acabar finalizando a Spann por ground and pound. Además, Felipe Lima (15-2) y Morgan Charriere (21-13-1) protagonizaron otro choque de estilos de ensueño que se llevó el peleador brasileño para debutar con éxito en el peso pluma de la UFC. The 40-year-old stormed to a unanimous decision victory to clinch the vacant WBC super-lightweight belt and bow out as a three-time undisputed world champion with 84,000 fans in attendance at Dublin's historic sporting home.

Taylor, an Olympic champion and two-weight undisputed champion, hangs up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest female boxer in history and a game-changing pioneer for women's sport.

articles.title: UFC Paris: Michael 'Venom' Page wins in underwhelming UFC farewell
articles.summary: Michael 'Venom' Page's last fight on his UFC contract ends in an underwhelming win against Nursulton Ruziboev amid booing fans in Paris.
articles.body:
Michael 'Venom' Page's last fight on his UFC contract ended in an underwhelming win against Nursulton Ruziboev amid booing fans in Paris.

London's Page, who is nicknamed 'MVP', landed a handful of eye-catching strikes during the contest but could not deliver the knockout that the fans craved as he won by unanimous decision.

The 39-year-old's victory means all five of his wins in the UFC since joining in 2024 have come via decision.

Page joined the UFC with a reputation as an innovative striker with a resume of highlight-reel knockouts, but admitted pre-fight he has underperformed since joining the organisation.

Page said the fight with Uzbekistan's Ruziboev was "important to re-establish myself with the UFC", but he did not get the finish he wanted.

Page, who arrived in the UFC over two years ago with 13 knockouts to his name, received a raucous ovation from the French crowd as he entered the octagon.

Ruziboev controlled the majority of the first round on the ground before Page started to open up midway through the fight.

He landed a kick to Ruziboev's knee which wobbled the 32-year-old, before smiling and showboating as he delivered a number of feints.

Page delivered an overhead right and an elbow, but the explosive moments were few and far between as the crowd grew frustrated at a lack of action.

Throughout the bout, Page landed only 12 significant strikes to Ruziboev's eight.

Page has shown throughout his UFC career he is a master of movement and evasion, without having the finishing instinct that the most successful fighters possess.

The fight against Ruziboev followed the same pattern, and although Page was awarded victory by the judges, his arm was raised after jeers from the crowd.

With Page now a free agent, potential options for him if he does not re-sign with the UFC include joining the PFL or turning to boxing.

There was also victory for fellow Briton Kurtis Campbell, who submitted American Trevor Peek in the third round of their featherweight bout via a rear-naked choke.

It was a return to winning ways for the 24-year-old Liverpudlian, who lost on his UFC debut to Danny Silva in March.

Campbell's win extends his professional record to nine wins and one defeat.

"I know my debut didn't go the way I wanted it to but I'm here to show I'm the real deal and the future is bright," said Campbell.

Earlier on the card, London's Nathaniel Wood lost by unanimous decision to Moldova's Pavel Andrusca, bringing his four-fight win streak to an end.

Andrusca, who was a late replacement after Wood's original opponent Mairon Santos withdrew 10 days prior to the fight, extended the unbeaten start to his career to nine.

At UFC 322 on 3 October in Salt Lake City, it was announced Brazil's Natalia Silva will fight for the vacant flyweight title against China's Wang Cong.

Former title holder Valentina Shevchenko has vacated the belt and is set to miss over a year with injury, according to the UFC.

articles.title: Taylor vs Pili: Boxing world pays tribute to 'one of the best to ever do it'
articles.summary: Some of the biggest names in women's boxing pay tribute to Katie Taylor after the Irish great ended her career with victory over Flora Pili at Croke Park.
articles.body:
Some of the biggest names in women's boxing have paid tribute to Katie Taylor after the Irish great ended her career with victory over Flora Pili at Croke Park .

Unified lightweight champion Caroline Dubois called Taylor "one of the best to ever do it", while Claressa Shields said the 40-year-old deserved to "ride off into the sunset".

Taylor beat Pili on points in Dublin to become undisputed light-welterweight champion and retires with 26 wins from 27 professional contests, Olympic gold and three undisputed title triumphs across two divisions.

"Thank you so much for paving the way," Londoner Dubois wrote on X. "Wishing you happiness, success and joy for this next season."

Taylor was sharper throughout, repeatedly beating the Frenchwoman to the punch before finishing with one final burst of combinations as the crowd rose to its feet.

American Shields - the self-proclaimed Greatest Woman of All Time - added: "Congrats Katie. Now ride off into the sunset. You deserve it all."

Super-featherweight champion Alycia Baumgardner described Taylor as "a trailblazer who helped set the stage for all of us".

"What a legacy," she wrote. "It's been a privilege watching your journey from the beginning."

'There will never be another one like her'

Taylor's farewell unfolded in front of more than 80,000 fans in Dublin, with Westlife performing before the main event and Croke Park providing a fitting backdrop to her final night.

Former world champion Carl Frampton said Taylor's relationship with the Irish public was unlike anything else in boxing.

"You can tell that she doesn't enjoy doing stuff in front of the media, but she still has this adulation from everybody," the Northern Irishman said.

"Katie Taylor is different, she's special and there will never be another one like her."

Former cruiserweight world champion Tony Bellew described the occasion as one of the most remarkable exits the sport had seen.

"I don't think in all of my years of watching this game, I have seen an exit as beautiful, amazing and fitting," he said.

"She has just retired as the greatest champion ever. I have never seen a fighter leave as an undisputed champion on their own terms."

Former world champion Barry Jones picked out the final 20 seconds, when Taylor produced the kind of rapid combinations which defined so many of her biggest fights.

"That's what you really remember about her," he said on the Dazn broadcast.

"Those rallies of big punches, combinations and that's how she finished her last fight."

American Mikaela Mayer - who was also ringside - was struck by the final image of Taylor placing her gloves in the centre of the ring.

"I was sitting there watching her put her gloves in the centre of the ring and it's like a story," she said.

Taylor had long dreamed of fighting at Croke Park and had made clear she wanted the stadium to stage the final chapter of her career.

Bellew said there was "no way" Taylor would return to boxing, although he could see her remaining involved by mentoring younger fighters.

"She will always be there to give her advice, speak to her and help her," he said.

"But ultimately she will sail off into the sunset and who could possibly deserve it more."

articles.title: Praias impróprias em Santos: Cetesb libera apenas um ponto para banho | G1
articles.standfirst: Boletim da Cetesb aponta 15 pontos impróprios entre os 71 analisados nas praias das oito cidades litorâneas da região. Bertioga e Peruíbe não têm locais com restrição.
articles.summary: O novo boletim da Cetesb indica que Santos tem seis praias impróprias para banho, enquanto Bertioga e Peruíbe seguem com todos os pontos liberados na Baixada Santista.
articles.body:
Praia de Santos (SP) chamou atenção com mancha escura ano mar — Foto: Matheus Müller/g1

Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, tem seis pontos impróprios para banho entre os sete analisados pela Companhia Ambiental do Estado de São Paulo (Cetesb), segundo boletim divulgado na última quinta-feira (3). Apenas o ponto de José Menino, na altura da Rua Frederico Ozanan, está próprio.

Ao todo, 71 pontos foram analisados nas praias das oito cidades litorâneas da Baixada Santista. Destes, 56 estão próprios para banho e 15 foram classificados como impróprios.

Além de Santos, há pontos impróprios em São Vicente, Praia Grande, Guarujá, Mongaguá e Itanhaém. Bertioga e Peruíbe não têm praias com restrição no levantamento. A próxima atualização está prevista para 10 de setembro.

A classificação da Cetesb é baseada na análise da quantidade de bactérias indicadoras de contaminação fecal encontrada na água. Para isso, são consideradas amostras coletadas durante cinco semanas consecutivas.

Nas praias de água salgada, a Cetesb analisa a presença de enterococos. O ponto é considerado impróprio quando duas das cinco amostras passam de 100 UFC por 100 ml de água ou quando a coleta mais recente ultrapassa 400 UFC por 100 ml.

Os locais impróprios recebem bandeira vermelha, enquanto aqueles considerados próprios para banho são sinalizados com bandeira verde.

A Cetesb recomenda evitar o banho de mar nos pontos classificados como impróprios. Segundo a companhia, o contato com água contaminada pode aumentar o risco de infecções e outras doenças. A orientação também é:

⚠️Tomar banho de mar nas primeiras 24 horas após chuvas intensas; ⚠️Banhar-se em canais, córregos ou rios que afluem às praias; ⚠️Engolir água do mar; ⚠️Levar animais de estimação à praia.

Segundo a Cetesb, a doença mais comum associada ao contato com água contaminada é a gastroenterite, que pode provocar enjoo, vômitos, dor de estômago, diarreia, dor de cabeça e febre.

Também podem ocorrer infecções nos olhos, ouvidos, nariz e garganta. A companhia aponta ainda risco de doenças como hepatite A, cólera e febre tifoide.

articles.title: “That is the only thing that I have fallen short of”: Michael Page gets honest after his UFC Paris win revealing what he feels has been missing all along
articles.summary: MMA News: Michael “Venom” Page walked away from UFC Paris with another win, yet the result carried more meaning than a number on his record. The British striker.
articles.body: Michael “Venom” Page walked away from UFC Paris with another win, yet the result carried more meaning than a number on his record. The British striker defeated Nursulton Ruziboev by unanimous decision after a difficult start. It was a solid performance from the veteran, though it did not bring the spectacular finish that has long been associated with his name. That makes Page’s earlier admission about his UFC career even more revealing.Michael Page feels he has fallen short of the “wow factor” that made him famousPage did not arrive in the UFC without a reputation.Long before making his promotional debut in 2024, he had already become one of the most recognizable fighters outside the organization. His Bellator career was built around an unusual striking style, quick movement and the ability to produce finishes that could leave fans stunned.The results have been respectable too. Page had lost only once in his first five UFC fights before facing Ruziboev. His defeat came against Ian Machado Garry in a razor-thin decision, while wins over Sharabutdin Magomedov and Jared Cannonier added some major names to his record.Still, Page has not been completely satisfied with the way his UFC story has developed.When asked if he was disappointed, the 39-year-old gave an unusually honest answer.“Yeah, it's definitely disappointing. It is a lot more difficult when you do not understand how you have gotten to this place because you do not know what you can change.”For Page, the frustration is not simply about his losses. He believes his performances have not always carried the same impact as the fights that made him famous before entering the UFC.That is where his most telling admission came.“I feel like that is the only thing that I have fallen short of. Although most of my fights have been entertaining, I feel like I have fallen short of that wow factor that I was known for.”It is a striking admission from a fighter whose reputation was built around making people wonder what he might do next.Page knows the UFC is filled with elite competition. He also understands that spectacular finishes are not guaranteed.“Obviously, we are in a game where guys are super talented. We are at the highest division, so it is never going to be a home run all the time.”That reality has not stopped him from wanting more.He still wants to create the kind of moments that made him such a popular fighter in the first place.Michael “Venom” Page’s UFC Paris win showed he can still adjust when the fight does not go his wayRuziboev gave Page a very different test in Paris.The British fighter did not have everything go his way from the opening bell. Ruziboev was able to make things difficult early, forcing Page to adjust instead of allowing him to settle into an easy striking rhythm.Page responded as an experienced fighter should.He stayed composed, found his range and grew into the contest. The fight eventually went to the judges, with Page earning a unanimous decision victory.It was another important win.It also offered an interesting contrast to what Page had said before the fight.He had already identified his lack of aggression as something he wanted to change. Looking back at his previous performances, Page believed he could have pushed the action more instead of waiting for the perfect opportunity.“Yeah, I guess potentially you can have regrets in retrospect,” he said.“With fights, you can learn from them. Everything else you cannot really control.”His solution was clear.“The main side of it would be to have a bit more output in some of my fights so that would be really trying to go for the win by being a bit more bloodthirsty.”That mindset makes the Paris performance particularly interesting.Page won the fight without needing to force a finish. He showed patience and the ability to recover from a challenging start. Those are valuable qualities, especially against an opponent who can create problems in multiple areas.Yet the fight also showed why Page continues to talk about the missing spark in his UFC career.The spectacular finish never came.Instead, he earned his victory through adjustments, striking and control over the later stages of the fight.There is nothing wrong with that approach. Fighters at this level cannot chase a knockout at every moment and risk throwing away a winnable fight.For Page, however, the standard is different because of what he has already accomplished.He knows what it feels like to produce moments that fans remember.He knows how quickly one perfect strike can change a fight.That is the version of himself he is still trying to bring back to the UFC stage.The Paris victory showed that Page remains capable of solving problems inside the cage. It also showed that the issue he openly identified before the fight has not completely disappeared.Now Page is looking for that feeling that once made his fights impossible to ignore.For the veteran, perhaps that is the real challenge ahead. Not simply winning more fights, but finding a way to make those wins feel unmistakably like Michael “Venom” Page.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Dam did him bad": Salahdine Parnasse stunned Dan Hooker in his UFC Paris debut as fighters react to a performance that changed everything
articles.summary: MMA News: Salahdine Parnasse could hardly have asked for a better UFC debut. Fighting Dan Hooker in the main event of UFC Paris, the French star needed only one.
articles.body: Salahdine Parnasse could hardly have asked for a better UFC debut. Fighting Dan Hooker in the main event of UFC Paris, the French star needed only one round to make his presence known. His finish impressed fighters watching from outside the Octagon, while Parnasse quickly showed that he has much bigger ambitions for his UFC run. What happened in Paris was more than a debut win. It was an arrival that immediately changed the conversation around him.Salahdine Parnasse turned one opening against Dan Hooker into a brutal first-round finishParnasse entered the UFC with plenty of attention already around him. The promotion had trusted him with a main-event spot in Paris, giving him a major opportunity in front of his home crowd.There was little time for him to settle in.The opening exchanges were measured, with both fighters using kicks and looking for openings. Parnasse did not appear interested in forcing the finish. Instead, he stayed composed and waited for Hooker to give him an opportunity.That moment arrived with a damaging body kick.Parnasse landed cleanly to Hooker's midsection, and the New Zealander immediately showed that the shot had affected him. Parnasse recognized the opening and moved forward. A head kick followed before the Frenchman unleashed a fast series of punches.Hooker could not find a way out.The referee stepped in at 2:35 of the first round, giving Parnasse a knockout victory in his UFC debut.The result was especially impressive because Parnasse managed to finish an experienced opponent without allowing the fight to become a long, difficult battle. He showed patience before suddenly switching gears when the opening appeared.That detail stood out to former UFC fighter Alan Jouban.Jouban reacted to the performance on social media, writing: “Wow. impressive performance. Patient, methodical and when he decided to go was able to finish it. #UFCParis”Jouban's reaction captured what made the finish stand out. Parnasse did not spend the entire fight chasing a knockout. He waited, found the right moment and then attacked with speed.Terrance McKinney also had a strong reaction to what he saw from the French newcomer. “Damn did him bad Parnasse welcome to rankings and the ufc 👏👏👏”McKinney's comment reflected the bigger conversation developing around Parnasse. A debut victory is one thing, but a first-round knockout over a respected UFC veteran can immediately change expectations.Belal Muhammad was already looking toward the next matchup. “Aight he’s getting Michael Chandler next”The comment added Michael Chandler to the growing list of possible opponents for Parnasse and showed just how quickly the conversation moved beyond his debut.The reactions painted a clear picture of the impact Parnasse's performance had. Jouban focused on his patience and timing. McKinney saw a fighter who had already done enough to enter the rankings conversation. Muhammad was already thinking about who could be next.For a newcomer, that is a significant shift.Salahdine Parnasse now has the attention of the lightweight division after his UFC arrivalParnasse was not finished making his intentions known once the fight ended.During his post-fight interview, the Frenchman made it clear that he wants to move quickly through the lightweight division. He said he was ready for a top-five opponent before naming Max Holloway as the matchup he wants most.Parnasse spoke about Holloway with clear respect, calling him a legend while insisting that he is ready to share the Octagon with him.The callout gives the UFC an interesting decision.Holloway has years of experience at the highest level and has faced some of the biggest names in the sport. A fight with Parnasse would therefore be a major step up for the Frenchman after only one UFC appearance.At the same time, Parnasse's performance gave him a strong argument for being tested against a recognizable opponent.Michael Chandler is another possibility after Muhammad's reaction. Chandler would present a different challenge, particularly because of his explosive wrestling, power and experience in high-level lightweight fights.The UFC may ultimately decide that Parnasse needs another fight before entering the top-five picture. One victory is still only one victory, even when it comes against an experienced fighter like Hooker.But Parnasse has already made one thing difficult to ignore.He does not look like a fighter who intends to spend years quietly climbing the UFC ladder.His journey to the promotion was already unusual. Parnasse had previously turned down opportunities to join the UFC before eventually making the move. When the opportunity finally came, he was placed directly into a major main-event spotlight in Paris.He responded with a finish that lasted less than three minutes.Now, the attention has shifted to what comes next.The reactions from Jouban, McKinney and Muhammad showed that Parnasse's debut was not viewed as just another UFC victory. His performance gave other fighters a reason to start discussing him immediately.That is perhaps the biggest change coming out of UFC Paris.Parnasse arrived with questions surrounding how quickly he could adjust to the UFC level. He left with those questions replaced by a different one: how far can he go from here?His first UFC fight could have simply been an introduction.Instead, it became a statement that has put Parnasse firmly on the lightweight division's radar.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Irish icon sails into retirement with the most perfect farewell
articles.summary: Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Irish icon Katie Taylor sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells at Dublin's towering Croke Park.
articles.body:
Katie Taylor addressed the Croke Park crowd as she paid tribute to her mother Bridget, but her extended family of 83,000 inside Croke Park and many more tuning in will have known this one was for them too.

Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Taylor is no ordinary fighter and her swansong proved as extraordinary as the fighter and person.

After 30 years lacing up the gloves, Taylor, 40, sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells in front of 83,000 adoring fans at Dublin's iconic Croke Park, just three miles from the scene of her first official bout 25 years earlier.

The final act in the ring was to sweep past Flora Pili to cement her legacy in Ireland and beyond, bowing out as a three-time and two-weight undisputed champion.

It was a night of celebration, cheers and plenty of tears as fans and peers turned out for her victory lap, showing love and appreciation for a career which thrilled and inspired in equal measure.

"It was everything I expected and more," Taylor said at her final post-fight news conference.

"Thankfully I was able to hold my emotions together tonight as I was getting emotional all week and the last few months' preparation was so emotional.

"The atmosphere was so special. I was beyond my wildest dreams - what a special night."

Taylor crowns career in stylish Croke Park triumph

Tears, blood & triumph - Taylor's iconic career in pictures

Before her hand could be raised in the ring, there were battles to be won outside of it.

Born in 1986 as the youngest of four children to former Irish champion father Peter and mother Bridget - one of Ireland's first female officials - the very notion of women's boxing in Ireland appeared fanciful.

While older brothers Lee and Peter were welcomed into the boxing fold, Katie became K from Bray - a girl hiding her identity to simply compete in an exclusively male environment.

The fighting spirit and determination which characterises her sporting prowess is as much a feature of her personality, and in 2001 as a 15-year-old she took part in the first sanctioned women's bout in Ireland since it was outlawed following future world champion Deirdre Gogarty's 1991 debut in Limerick.

Perhaps fitting, as five years earlier, Taylor wrote to role model Gogarty, expressing frustration at the lack of opportunities to compete and outlining her dreams of one day being allowed to compete at the Olympic Games.

Prophetic words, as it was her exceptional talent on display in front of International Olympic Committee members in 2007 which convinced them to add women's boxing to the programme for London 2012.

All eyes were on her as Katie mania grew throughout the Games - her victory over Sofya Ochigava in the lightweight final a moment of national sporting joy comparable to the heady days of Jack Charlton's Republic of Ireland teams at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups - the Excel arena transformed into a small corner of Ireland on an unforgettable day.

A recognised star in Irish boxing circles was now a household name, her humble and gracious manner winning the hearts of a nation that has remained firmly in her corner.

"The 'ole ole oles' carried me all over the world: to Leeds, to Manchester, Brooklyn, Boston, Dallas, Manhattan," she reflected.

"This night is so special because I wanted to put on a performance for them. I don't think it was a career-best performance, but I got the win for them, just to say 'thank you'."

Her star did not dim despite a disappointing Rio Games in 2016, and while Matchroom boss Eddie Hearn took convincing to take a punt on her as a professional, the faith has been repaid in spades.

Within three years, Taylor was undisputed champion at lightweight, rising from undercard to centre stage as she carried out her promise to do for women's professional boxing what she had achieved as an amateur, all to a chorus of the aforementioned 'ole ole oles' from the support which followed her every move.

A seminal night in 2022 saw her defeat Amanda Serrano at a sold-out Madison Square Garden in a fight of the year contender - the first time a women's bout had headlined the famous arena, a major turning point for the female code.

They would trade leather a further two times after Taylor had avenged her sole professional career defeat by Chantelle Cameron to become a two-weight champion.

Perhaps that was the perfect way to sign off, but the Croke Park itch had to be scratched and while those gates seemed destined to remain locked, Taylor's status made it happen.

Could she fill such a vast stadium? Of course. Perhaps the doubters did not grasp the reverence in which the softly spoken yet inspirational woman from Bray is held.

While her trophy cabinet is overflowing with gold medals and world title belts, perhaps her greatest legacy is leaving women's boxing in a vastly better place than she found it - that Serrano trilogy lifting women's boxing to new heights.

Taylor broke through the barriers with a grace which belied the obstacles she faced yet her quiet determination and humble nature will serve as an example of what can be achieved by belief, hard work and a refusal to accept her lot as young girls can now walk the path she laid.

Fierce inside the ring yet unassuming outside of it - even factoring in an impulse-buy speedboat, since sold - superlatives such as trailblazer, icon and Ireland's greatest sportsperson are not hyperbolic, for Taylor's status as a legend is in no way cliched.

She has indicated she will remain in the sport, but for now, there is time to savour an extraordinary career, with her place among boxing's greats set in stone.

Irish boxing is going to be a lesser place.

"I'm retired now so I can eat what I want, but I'm just going to enjoy a nice celebration and look back on a dream ending to a dream career.

"My story is the story of everyone in this room: we all have our ups and downs. I think people resonate with your vulnerabilities and your successes - saw me cope with the heartbreak of Rio, the Chantelle Cameron loss and personal difficulties.

"My story is the story of everyone in this room."
