articles.title: Ireland’s boxing great Katie Taylor bows out as undisputed champion
articles.summary: The 40-year-old retained her WBA, IBF and WBO super-lightweight belts to become the undisputed champion for third time.
articles.body:
Boxing great Katie Taylor has signed off on a glorious, title-laden career that blazed the trail for women’s boxing in her native Ireland and around the world with a win over France’s Flora Pili in Dublin.

Taylor brought the curtain down with a points victory in front of 80,000 adoring fans at Croke Park on Saturday.

The 40-year-old retained her WBA, IBF and WBO super-lightweight belts and added the vacant WBC title to become the undisputed champion for a third time on Saturday.

Taylor emerged for her final ring walk to a deafening reception from the sold-out crowd, with fireworks, light shows and chants of “Katie, Katie, Katie!” echoing around the home of Irish Gaelic sports.

She used her superior movement and timing to control much of the early and middle rounds, but the resilient Pili refused to fade.

The previously unbeaten 29-year-old French challenger came back strongly in the seventh, giving Taylor her most difficult round, before the Irishwoman steadied herself in the eighth and reasserted control.

As the crowd erupted into chants of “Ole! Ole! Ole!”, Taylor raised her arms and embraced Pili after the final bell.

The judges awarded Taylor a unanimous decision.

Afterwards, Taylor thanked her family, including her father, who taught her “how to fight”, and hugged her tearful mother.

The victory completed a remarkable journey for Taylor, who began boxing at a time when girls were barred from amateur competition in Ireland and sometimes entered bouts simply as “K Taylor”.

She went on to win Olympic lightweight gold at London 2012, when women’s boxing made its games debut, before turning professional four years later.

Taylor finishes her professional career with 26 victories and one defeat, having won world titles at lightweight and super-lightweight.

Her farewell also brought top-level boxing back to Croke Park for the first time since Muhammad Ali defeated Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972.

articles.title: Katie Taylor ecstatic after beating Flora Pili to make perfect end to ‘dream career’ at Dublin's Croke Park
articles.summary: Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972.
articles.body:
Taylor outclassed Flora Pili in a unanimous points victory in front of a crowd of 80,000 to ensure her three decades as an amateur and professional boxer ended in fairytale fashion.

Wild celebrations followed the announcement that she had overwhelmed the previously unbeaten Pili 100-90 100-90 98-91 on the scorecards.

For Taylor the feeling of signing off in front of her fans bettered winning Olympic gold at London 2012, headlining Madison Square Garden and her trilogy against Amanda Serrano.

The 40-year-old said: "This was definitely the highlight of my whole career.

"I didn't think anything could get bigger than London 2012 and then MSG came along.

"I didn't think anything could get bigger than that first fight with Serrano and then here we are at Croke Park.

"I ended my career on top, like every athlete wants to do, on my terms, and I ended it as the undisputed champion.

"That's exactly how I wanted it to end. It was so important to me all along to end my career well."

Taylor thrilled Croke Park with a spine-tingling ring walk and also delivered in the ring by outclassing Pili across all 10 rounds.

She finished the fight by launching an all-out assault in the final 10 seconds that was roared on by the crowd and once the bell sounded, she smiled and hugged her opponent knowing she had thrown her final shots.

Taylor said: "This night was everything I expected and more. Thankfully I was able to hold my emotions together because I was getting emotional all week speaking about this event.

"And over the last few months, the preparation for this has been so emotional. But the atmosphere was so special. It was beyond my wildest dreams. It was unbelievable.

"What an amazing night. Looking back on an amazing career, this was just a dream ending to a dream career for me. What a way to end.

"I don't think there's another country in the world that would sell 80,000 tickets for a female athlete. I'm convinced Ireland was the only country that would actually do that.

"What a way to end this amazing journey. I started off this career and I had the dream of becoming an Olympic champion.

"I achieved that, but then these last 10 years have been beyond my wildest dreams. It's been a remarkable 10 years."

Hearn: Greatest Irish sportsperson of all time

"We went into this event and I said this will be the greatest atmosphere and greatest occasion boxing has ever seen and Croke Park, you did it tonight.

"There were 83,000 people in here tonight and they are still here. I wasn't supposed to do something we haven't done before. This is a woman who refused to take no as an answer and banged on every door. She's the greatest Irish sportsperson of all time.

"She made this happen. She made it happen because the entire nation supported her so proudly."

articles.title: La irlandesa Katie Taylor gana su combate de despedida ante 80.000 personas en Croke Park
articles.standfirst: Una de las boxeadoras más grandes de todos los tiempos se retira a los 40 años con 26 victorias y una sola derrota
articles.summary: Una de las boxeadoras más grandes de todos los tiempos se retira a los 40 años con 26 victorias y una sola derrota
articles.body: Katie Taylor puso fin a su extraordinaria carrera con una victoria contundente sobre la francesa y hasta ayer invicta Flora Pili ante 80.000 aficionados en Croke Park (Dublín). La irlandesa, oro olímpico en el estreno del boxeo femenino en Londres 2012, cumplió su último deseo: pelear en la catedral deportiva de Irlanda. Taylor, de 40 años, dominó a su oponente durante los 10 asaltos, obteniendo una victoria por decisión unánime y retirándose como campeona indiscutible de las 140 libras (63,503 kg). Taylor (26-1) sumó el título vacante de peso superligero del CMB a sus cinturones de la OMB, la AMB y la FIB. Las puntuaciones de los jueces fueron 100-90, 100-90 y 98-91. El récord de Pili es de 12-1 con esta derrota. En abril de 2022, Taylor venció a Amanda Serrano en un Madison Square Garden abarrotado, en lo que fue el primer combate de boxeo femenino en encabezar el cartel del recinto. Ambas se han enfrentado tres veces en total, con Taylor victoriosa en todas las ocasiones, la más reciente en 2025. Esa trilogía es lo más icónico de su increíble carrera. Esta última victoria culminó una trayectoria extraordinaria para Taylor, quien comenzó a boxear en una época en la que las chicas tenían prohibido competir como aficionadas en Irlanda y a veces participaban en combates simplemente como "K Taylor". La irlandesa, que hizo su debut como profesional en 2016, se retira con 26 victorias (6 por KO) y una sola derrota, la sufrida ante la estadounidense Chantelle Cameron en su salto al peso superligero tras haber dominado ampliamente el ligero. Aquello ocurrió el 20 de mayo de 2023 y apenas medio año después y en el mismo escenario, el 3Arena de Dublín, Taylor se tomaba cumplida revancha. Tras el combate, la irlandesa colocó sus guantes en el centro del ring para simbolizar su retirada, mientras su equipo la ayudaba a colocar los cinturones alrededor de ellos. Tras el combate, dirigiéndose a la multitud eufórica, dijo: “¡Croke Park! ¡Lo logramos! El pueblo de Irlanda me dio un final de ensueño para una carrera de ensueño. Nada puede superar esto. Sin duda, este fue el momento culminante de toda mi carrera”. “Comencé mi carrera con el sueño de convertirme en campeona olímpica. Lo logré, pero estos últimos 10 años han superado mis expectativas más optimistas. Han sido 10 años extraordinarios”, finalizó Taylor.

articles.title: Video: UFC veteran floors man during police stop in Florida
articles.summary: Marlon Moraes recently returned to MMA with a win in Brazil
articles.body:
Marlon Moraes returned to the winning column in MMA recently in Brazil, when he won a decision against Maximiliano Perez in the main event of Liga Monstro Combate on August. 28, and a body cam video of his work as a policeman in Florida has gone viral days later.

Moraes, who works as a cop in South Florida, had to put his martial arts knowledge to use during a traffic stop on March 27. A man became confrontational against Moraes, calling him a "b*tch" and saying "I can f*ck you up". Moraes warned the man not to take another step in his direction, and immediately floored him once he did.

Moraes, a former WSOF bantamweight champion and UFC title contender, walked away from the sport in 2023 with a record of 23-13-1. He teased a return after signing with GFL, but eventually competed again in 2026 this past August to snap a seven-fight losing skid.

Moraes told MMA Fighting he's not retired, and plans on seeking a deal to fight again in the United States.

articles.title: Fabià Sintes, exultante tras el UFC París: "Como soy del Atlético había que ganar sufriendo"
articles.standfirst: El peleador español se mostró muy contento tras su exitoso debut en la compañía ante Michael Aljarouj
articles.summary: El peleador español se mostró muy contento tras su exitoso debut en la compañía ante Michael Aljarouj
articles.body: Fabià Sintes fue uno de los grandes nombres del UFC París del día de ayer. El peleador español debutaba en la compañía con el cartel de campeón de peso mosca de WOW FC, y demostró su talento venciendo por decisión unánime a Michael Aljarouj. Al acabar el combate, 'El Potro Menorquín' se mostró exultante, y lo único que lamentó fue no haber podido finalizar la pelea en un segundo asalto donde tuvo varias oportunidades para hacerlo. Como es normal en un día así, Fabià empezó la pelea con nervios. Aljarouj era el ídolo local, había mucha presión sobre sus hombros y en el primer round no logró dominar todo lo que le gustaría. Eso sí, en el segundo asalto consiguió dominar al galo en el suelo y dio un clínic de MMA. Le cortó la cara con buenos codos y estuvo a pocos segundos de someterlo con una guillotina que habría sido el cúlmen a una noche de ensueño. Por si fuera poco, en el tercer asalto también dominó hasta los últimos dos minutos, lo que le sirvió para llevarse la victoria por decisión unánime y ganarse un puesto en la compañía de MMA más importante del planeta. "Me he visto bien. Yo creía que había ganado el primer asalto. El segundo me he visto muy bien, he dominado, he tenido un par de posiciones de finalización... Y el tercero ha sido igual salvo los últimos minutos, que he sufrido un poco. Como soy del Atlético de Madrid hay que ganar sufriendo", le dijo a Álvaro Colmenero en una entrevista con Eurosport al finalizar la pelea. Esta victoria de Fabià no solo es importante para él, ya que es un paso de gigante en su carrera, sino para las MMA españolas. En los últimos meses se ha vivido el despido de Dani Bárez de la compañía, la primera derrota profesional de Ilia Topuria y dos derrotas muy dolorosas de Joel Álvarez, por lo que este resultado es un rayo de esperanza en un año muy difícil para los nuestros. También es una prueba del gran talento que hay en España, ya que se suma al exitoso debut de Hecher Sosa a principios de año y da motivos a la UFC para venir finalmente a España después de muchos meses llamando a la puerta. Fabià no solo ganó, sino que dominó a todo un campeón de Hexagone que era la cara A del combate al pelear frente a su gente. Por tanto, lo normal es que la compañía le ofrezca un contrato de varias peleas y le veamos volver al octágono de la UFC una vez se recupere de las secuelas de esta batalla. En una división como la de peso mosca que ha ganado enteros durante los últimos tiempos ahora se une un hombre muy entretenido de ver, que siempre busca finalizar y ha demostrado que merece estar junto a los mejores del mundo.

articles.title: Video: Former UFC title challenger plants man on ground during traffic stop
articles.summary: Dumb idea alert: challenging a former UFC headliner working as a police officer.
articles.body:
Former UFC title challenger Marlon Moraes is working as a police officer in Florida, and one traffic stop subject found that out the hard way.

In a recent viral body cam video, Moraes, who works for the Coral Springs Police Department (Fla.), is seen being verbally challenged by a man who was pulled over in a parking lot. The man told Moraes, "You can't do sh*t," only to discover the opposite was true.

Moraes displayed patience until the man took a step toward him, at which point he tripped the man to the pavement and other officers assisted in putting him in handcuffs.

The incident took place March 27 but just recently came to light online. It's unclear what the man is alleged to have done that caused him to be pulled over to begin with.

Moraes, 38, has worked as a South Florida police officer since 2024. He retired from MMA in 2023 but announced a comeback in 2025. He won for the first time in seven years Aug. 28 when he defeated Maximilliano Perez by unanimous decision at LMC 2 in Brazil.

Moraes is best known for being a UFC bantamweight title challenger and former World Series of Fighting (WSOF) bantamweight champion.

articles.title: Colby Covington not 'fully retired,' open to return if UFC offers right fight
articles.summary: Colby Covington hasn't fully closed the door on MMA.
articles.body:
Colby Covington may not be all done in MMA.

Despite announcing his retirement in May, the former UFC title challenger is still leaving the door open for another go in the octagon. Covington revealed to MMA Junkie that the main reason he retired was so he could aggressively pursue his wrestling career in Real American Freestyle – something he couldn't do as an active UFC fighter.

Covington is 4-0 under RAF and recently claimed the inaugural RAF Cruiserweight Crossover Championship with a win over top UFC lightweight contender Arman Tsarukyan .

"I'm technically retired, technically, but that was just the red proverbial tape I needed to get by so I could get the biggest matchups in RAF," Covington told MMA Junkie. "Everybody knows my first love and passion was always wrestling. My dad got me into wrestling as a kid; it was a family business. He wrestled his whole life. His family, his dad wrestled, so I was just following in the lineage of the generations, following the family tree in the wrestling business. It was always my first true love and passion."

Covington's retirement from MMA might've surprised some, as he was looking to fight at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June. But with him not getting a spot on the card and not seeing interesting matchups outside of fighting at the White House, Covington just thought it would make more sense to focus on RAF, where he's also an investor.

"I wasn't getting any fights in the UFC," Covington said. "They weren't really offering me the fights that I want. I didn't get on the White House card. I really wanted to be on the White House card; I would have done anything to be on that card and would have fought anybody. I would have fought a heavyweight. It didn't matter. I just wanted to compete there in front of the greatest president of all time, Donald Trump, but it never transpired. So, you know, I don't think that I'm technically retired, but it's just what needed to happen so I could wrestle guys like Arman, so I could wrestle guys like Belal (Muhammad), so I could wrestle guys like (Kamaru) Usman, so I could wrestle all these big marquee matchups in RAF and get back to my first true love and passion, which is wrestling.

"So I don't know, maybe I come back for a fight. I wouldn't say I'm fully retired. Everybody keeps saying, 'Oh, he's retired.' You must not see what I'm doing in RAF. I'm smoking, dudes. I just beat the number one contender in lightweight and that was light work. I made it look easy ... I'm still in my prime. I'm still taking good care of my body and my brain, so I wouldn't say the door is fully closed and I'm retired. I would just say that we're on a temporary break as I pursue my interest and first love and passion for wrestling at the RAF."

Just as Covington is not committing to retirement, he's also not committing to fighting again. He thinks never setting foot in the octagon is a possibility, and he's fine with that. Covington won an interim UFC title and challenged for the undisputed title three times. He's at peace with what he's done in the sport.

"Yeah, how could I not be at peace? I reached the mountaintop," Covington said. "Not a lot of people are ever going to win a world title in the UFC. You want to call it an interim title? Whatever. The active champion, I ended up beating his ass and leaving him on a stretcher, so I was the champion. People know I was the undisputed champion. I reached the mountaintop. I did it all. At what point do you need to walk away? At what point are you just going to keep taking punches and keep coming back to fight?

"I was never going to be one of those guys that was going to fight in his 40s. It just wasn't going to happen. I've seen too many times guys come through our gym, and they fight late in age, and they get seriously hurt. That was never going to happen to me. I'm willing to entertain big and huge offers from the UFC and big fights. But if not, you know, it's OK. I'm at peace."
